subject: Request: temporary uptime tolerance and monthly credit bridge for StratoPay deployment
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@stratopay.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: StratoPay — service commitment discussion

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the onboarding walkthrough last week. We're prepping our production cutover in late August and I wanted to surface a concern up-front: our initial traffic ramp is expected to have several high-frequency windows as we migrate a subset of payment validation flows (attached: StratoPay_traffic_projection_JulAug.xlsx).

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood offer a temporary uptimes tolerance during the first 90 days so we can safely ramp without repeated hard failures?
- If uptime dips happen during that period, can we agree a capped monthly credit construct rather than the standard SLA remedy wording? Our procurement/legal team prefers a predictable credit bridge while we stabilize.

If useful, we can share more detail on expected spike cadence — happy to take a 30-min call this week. Also looping in our legal inbox (legal@stratopay.com) for visibility.

Best,
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform Partnerships
StratoPay

Attachments: StratoPay_traffic_projection_JulAug.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@stratopay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StratoPay — service commitment discussion

Hi Sarah — thanks for the projection, that helps.

We can absolutely put a short-term operational accommodation in place while you mature traffic patterns. High level we see two practical approaches (both presuming canary ramping and telemetry hooks):

Option A — Standard SLA, proactive tuning
- Keep standard uptime commitment (99.95%)
- Provide a one-time onboarding playbook: rate-limit recommendations, KV cache patterns, and a short burst-config to reduce tail failure modes
- Monthly credits per standard SLA if thresholds are missed (no temporary tolerance)

Option B — Temporary tolerance + credit bridge (recommended for aggressive ramps)
- For an initial 90-day onboarding window: maintain an operational target of 99.5% (soft target, not permanent)
- If uptime falls between 99.5% and 99.95%, Redwood will apply a capped monthly credit equal to up to 5% of that month’s Redwood invoice (credit bridge). If uptime falls below 99.5% we fall back to the standard SLA remedy ladder.
- Daily incident reporting during the window and a joint weekly checkpoint.

I attached a short draft waiver and a worked example of how the credit bridge would look across three ramp scenarios. Those attachments: provisioned-uptime-waiver-draft.pdf, credit-bridge-examples.xlsx.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tell us whether you prefer Option A or B.
2) If Option B, Sarah — confirm StratoPay legal can accept a capped-credit formula (we can reduce cap if needed).
3) Schedule a 30-min alignment on Tuesday 8/4 to agree telemetry and canary cadence.

Happy to adjust the percentages/cap if procurement pushes back — we want predictability for both sides.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: provisioned-uptime-waiver-draft.pdf (pdf, 28 KB); credit-bridge-examples.xlsx (xlsx, 18 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-02T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StratoPay — service commitment discussion

Olga — quick internal note before you finalize:
- I recommend we tighten the maximum credit cap to 3% of monthly invoice rather than 5%. 5% feels high for a temporary window and sets a bad precedent for larger enterprise contracts.
- Add a hard dollar ceiling as well (suggest $50,000) to avoid runaway exposure in month 1.
- Require daily incident report (which you already called out) and a clause that allows Redwood to pause the tolerance window early if we see systemic risk.
- Flag product to enable aggressive KV cache and prefix caching for their main traffic path; Connor can coordinate implementation.

If you go with that wording I’ll back it in pricing committee.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Pricing
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@stratopay.com>, legal@stratopay.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-05T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StratoPay — service commitment discussion

Hi Sarah & StratoPay Legal,

Thanks for the context and the projection sheet. We’re supportive of a short-term operational accommodation to help StratoPay safely ramp. A few legal points and proposed redlines are attached (redlined-SLA-stratopay.pdf):

- We can agree to a 90-day \"Onboarding Tolerance\" with a 99.5% operational target as described.
- Monthly credit cap: 3% of the Redwood invoice for that month OR $50,000, whichever is lower. Credits only apply to uptime between 99.5% and 99.95%.
- If uptime falls below 99.5%, standard SLA remedies apply.
- During the tolerance window StratoPay must: (a) execute the agreed canary ramp schedule, (b) provide daily traffic/incident feed to Redwood, and (c) accept our remedial tuning recommendations. Failure to follow the ramp plan will void the tolerance window.
- We’ll add an early-exit clause allowing Redwood to terminate the tolerance window if ongoing incidents indicate systemic instability that threatens other customers.

If this is acceptable, please have StratoPay Legal confirm and we'll produce a clean amendment and a redlined SLA for signature. Also happy to review the redline on a quick call if preferred.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlined-SLA-stratopay.pdf (pdf, 34 KB)
